author: Lauren Martinez
title: Why FBI dropped Amy Bradley case after she was 'found' 20 years ago - NewsBreak
text: Many have been clamoring for Amy Bradley to be found, with her family also allegedly seeking Kim Kardashian’s help after a Netflix docuseries shed new light on the case–but she may have already been “found” 20 years ago. Bradley’s disappearance from a Royal Caribbean cruise ship in 1998 has sparked intense new interest after the Netflix release of Amy Bradley is Missing, which introduced some to the case for the first time. Bradley was last seen on the balcony of her stateroom by her father, but disappeared without a trace 30 minutes later–and hasn’t been seen since. Since then, there have been endless theories about what happened to her, with suspicion cast on a band member she was seen with previously, concerns she was taken and sold to sex traffickers, and even those who think she fell overboard and died. With no true consensus, it’s been said, “ questions will remain” until everyone is in agreement about what happened to her . READ MORE: Amy Bradley's brother reveals major update in the case after Netflix documentary READ MORE: New Amy Bradley leads emerge following Netflix documentary 27 years later One of the most popular theories, however, is that she is still alive and has been in the Caribbean the entire time. Several “sightings” of her were shared throughout the years, though none panned out as leads. In 2005, Amy’s parents and brother received photos from an anonymous source, which claimed to be updated images of Amy. The images showed a woman called Jas, who was a sex worker for hire on a website based in the Caribbean, and in the Netflix series, her mother, Iva, admitted that they felt the photos were of Amy, due to major similarities in the two women’s faces. “Seeing the photos, it was a terrible thing. A level of panic. All I could keep thinking is, ‘Is that my daughter?’ We all looked at it–the nose, the chin and the hair–it took my breath away.’” Though and FBI analysis did determine the woman in the images was Amy, the IP address for the site couldn’t be tracked–and the FBI was unable to use it to find her. In an interview with The Hollywood Reporter, director Ari Mark said the FBI did exhaust all the options they had to look into the pictured–but nothing came of it. “[What’s] hard to ignore is how seriously the FBI took that photo,” he said. “It wasn’t like they were like, ‘Oh, whatever,’ they really did chase that down,” he continued. “They analysed the bed frame, tried to figure out where it was made.” “They sent an operative down there to actually scope it out. And they did look into that website, and they brought in that trafficking expert–it’s hard to ignore.” Because the IP address couldn’t be traced, no one was charged in relation to the photos–and Amy remained missing. Now, 20 years later, she remains on the FBI’s Most Wanted Missing Persons list.
